samples.summary: No test covers the table `columnWidths` cap on the live slides read path
samples.evidence: The shared band caps `data.columnWidths` at `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` (`packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:72-77`, asserted in `packages/slides/test/model/band-numerics.test.ts:122-145` and in the backend `PUT` spec). But `YorkieSlidesStore.readElement` does NOT call `bandElementNumerics`; it calls its own private `bandElementText` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:528-547, invoked at :638), which bands shape text and table cell bodies only and never touches `columnWidths`. The new frontend suite `packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.test.ts` adds tests for text bodies, shape text, table cell bodies, notes, layouts and masters, but grep for `columnWidths`/`MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` in that file returns zero matches. So the primary live reader of a collaborator-written deck has no test for the cap the rest of the change treats as load-bearing (a million-entry `columnWidths` is a hung paint for every viewer), and the gap is exactly what a test here would have surfaced.

samples.summary: `sanitizeDocStyles` is unit-tested, but neither read boundary that now calls it is
samples.evidence: `sanitizeDocStyles` itself has good unit coverage (`packages/docs/test/model/named-styles.test.ts:767-818`). The change wires it into two readers — `docsTreeToDocument` (crdt-tree.ts, the `opts.stylesJson` branch) and `YorkieDocStore.getStyles` (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:827`) — and neither call site has a test: grep for `docsTreeToDocument` across the repo finds only source files (no test file references it), and grep for `stylesJson`/`getStyles` in `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` finds nothing. Dropping either call would leave every test green while a peer-written `stylesJson` of `{"normal":{"inline":{"fontSize":1e9}}}` reaches every run's base style unbanded — the document-wide bypass the sanitizer exists to close. Note the frontend has no `tsc` lane either, so nothing else guards that wiring.
searchedFor: grep -r docsTreeToDocument packages (source files only, no tests)

samples.summary: `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH` recursion cap has no test, unlike its docs twin
samples.evidence: `bandElementNumerics` recurses through `data.children` and caps at `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH = 32` (band-numerics.ts:40, 112-117), justified in comment as "a band that blew the stack would be its own denial of service". The docs counterpart `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH` gets an explicit 20000-deep test (`packages/docs/test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts`, "caps its own recursion instead of blowing the stack"). `packages/slides/test/model/band-numerics.test.ts` tests only master styles and table columnWidths — it never exercises the group branch at all, let alone at depth; grep for `depth`/`nest`/`MAX_GROUP_DEPTH` under packages/slides/test finds no band-numerics test. The only group coverage is a single-level group child in the board-store test. So a regression removing the depth guard (or the group recursion entirely) would ship green.

samples.summary: `bandLayoutNumerics` staticElements, and `bandSlidesDocumentNumerics`' layouts/masters branches, are untested
samples.evidence: `bandLayoutNumerics` walks both `placeholders` and `staticElements` (band-numerics.ts:130-134); only `placeholders` is covered (frontend slides store test 'bands a layout placeholder spec a peer poisoned'). `bandSlidesDocumentNumerics` walks slides elements, notes, layouts and masters (band-numerics.ts:208-230), but the new snapshot-adapter tests (`packages/frontend/src/components/history/__tests__/snapshot-adapters.test.ts`, 'the revision-preview numeric band') assert only slide elements and notes for slides, and elements for board — no snapshot fixture carries a poisoned layout or master. Those branches could be deleted with the suite still green.
searchedFor: read the snapshot-adapters test hunk in the diff

samples.summary: Three new `normalizeListLevel` call sites (PDF painter, table renderer, peer cursor) have no poisoned-level test
samples.evidence: The change normalizes `listLevel` at six read sites. Coverage exists for the layout indent, `computeListCounters`, the markdown serializer and the editor paint pass (`packages/docs/test/model/list-level.test.ts`, and editor-tab-bullet.test.ts 'a poisoned list level paints inside the page'). The diff's own comment concedes the other three are "left to the unit test of the band itself": `pdf-painter.ts:367` and `:593`, `table-renderer.ts:525` (where the level is also a Map key — a NaN key never matches itself on reset) and `peer-cursor.ts:255,:395`. None of `packages/docs/test/export/pdf-exporter.test.ts`, `test/view/table-renderer.test.ts` exercises a non-finite/huge level, so a site wired to the raw value would still ship — the export path in particular fails for every reader of the document, not just the writer.
searchedFor: grep listLevel in packages/docs/test (18 files listed; checked pdf-exporter.test.ts, table-renderer.test.ts, list-level.test.ts)

samples.summary: Two new validator tests assert only `not.toThrow()`, so they cannot distinguish a working band from a destructive one
samples.evidence: 'treats null as absent, the way every other field here does' (validation.spec, the `deckWithFontSize(null)` case) and 'leaves a master without placeholder styles alone' assert nothing but the absence of a throw. The first would pass whether `fontSize: null` is left alone, deleted, or rewritten; the second would pass even if `bandMasterPlaceholderStyles` wiped the master object. Both would be discriminating with one assertion on the resulting value (e.g. `expect(...style.fontSize).toBeUndefined()`, `expect(deck.masters[0]).toEqual(input)`).

samples.summary: `FONT_SIZE_MAX = Math.min(400, MAX_FONT_SIZE)` states an invariant nothing asserts
samples.evidence: The new doc comment makes the picker ceiling's relationship to the model band load-bearing ("must stay at or under the model's"), but no test asserts `FONT_SIZE_MAX <= MAX_FONT_SIZE` or that `clampFontSize` output survives `normalizeFontSize` unchanged. The `Math.min` makes it true today by construction, so this is cosmetic — but the invariant is the kind that drifts when the picker constant is later edited to a literal.

finding.summary: No test covers the table `columnWidths` cap on the live slides read path
finding.evidence: The shared band caps `data.columnWidths` at `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` (`packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:72-77`, asserted in `packages/slides/test/model/band-numerics.test.ts:122-145` and in the backend `PUT` spec). But `YorkieSlidesStore.readElement` does NOT call `bandElementNumerics`; it calls its own private `bandElementText` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:528-547, invoked at :638), which bands shape text and table cell bodies only and never touches `columnWidths`. The new frontend suite `packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.test.ts` adds tests for text bodies, shape text, table cell bodies, notes, layouts and masters, but grep for `columnWidths`/`MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` in that file returns zero matches. verdict.reason: The reviewer's facts are accurate — `YorkieSlidesStore.readElement` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:638) calls the private `bandElementText` (:528-543), which bands shape text and table cell bodies but never `data.columnWidths`, and nothing downstream caps it (table-renderer.ts:86-92 allocates nCols+1 straight from the array). But that makes this a MISSING IMPLEMENTATION on the frontend read path, not a missing test for an implemented behavior: a test asserting a capped `columnWidths` from `store.read()` would fail today, so demanding it is demanding the band be added — squarely the correctness lens's lane ("whether the non-test code is correct" is explicitly excluded from mine), and the correctness reviewer already holds this exact item (.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:16). The behavior the diff actually added — the `columnWidths` cap in `bandTableColumnWidths` (band-numerics.ts:72-77) — does have meaningful, non-vacuous tests on both paths where it runs: band-numerics.test.ts:122-145 and docs-content.controller.spec.ts:1481-1525, each feeding `[100, Infinity, -5, 'wide', ...400]` and asserting length 256 / `[100,0,0,0]`. The frontend suite is scoped `describe('YorkieSlidesStore — the text-body numeric band')` (yorkie-slides-store.test.ts:840) and exercises every behavior `bandElementText` performs (:876-933), so there is no vacuous assertion, no over-mocking, and no changed behavior on that path left uncovered. Real issue, wrong lens — out of scope for test-adequacy.

finding.summary: `sanitizeDocStyles` is unit-tested, but neither read boundary that now calls it is
finding.evidence: `sanitizeDocStyles` itself has good unit coverage (`packages/docs/test/model/named-styles.test.ts:767-818`). The change wires it into two readers — `docsTreeToDocument` (crdt-tree.ts, the `opts.stylesJson` branch) and `YorkieDocStore.getStyles` (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:827`) — and neither call site has a test: grep for `docsTreeToDocument` across the repo finds only source files (no test file references it), and grep for `stylesJson`/`getStyles` in `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` finds nothing. Dropping either call would leave every test green while a peer-written `stylesJson` of `{"normal":{"inline":{"fontSize":1e9}}}` reaches every run's base style unbanded — the document-wide bypass the sanitizer exists to close. Note the frontend has no `tsc` lane either, so nothing else guards that wiring.
searchedFor: grep -r docsTreeToDocument packages (source files only, no tests)

verdict.reason: No test in the repo fails if `sanitizeDocStyles` is dropped from either read boundary. The boundaries ARE reached by tests (contrary to the reviewer's grep detail): `parseDocsSnapshot` -> `docsTreeToDocument` (snapshot-adapters.ts:178-179, tested at snapshot-adapters.test.ts:325-354) and `readDocsRoot` -> `docsTreeToDocument` (backend docs-tree.ts:250-251, tested at docs-tree.spec.ts:338-365), plus `getDocStyles`/`readDocStyles` in the frontend store (editor-undo-selection.test.ts:1121-1171). But every one of those assertions is satisfied with or without the sanitizer: the snapshot fixture registry is `{"Normal":{"fontSize":11,"fontFamily":"Arial"}}` (an unrecognised key the sanitizer passes through untouched), the `stylesJson: 5` case is stopped earlier by the `typeof` guard at crdt-tree.ts:319, the backend round-trip uses only in-band values, and the undo tests use valid style defs. Repo-wide greps for a poisoned registry (`1e9`/`Infinity` inside an `inline`/`block` entry, `stylesJson` in any test, `sanitizeDocStyles` outside its unit test) turn up nothing; notably yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3550-3641 has a numeric-band suite for tree attributes but no registry case. So the sanitizer's wiring at both new call sites is exercised-but-unasserted, i.e. no meaningful coverage, and its silent removal would let one peer-writable LWW string bypass normalizeFontSize/normalizeLineHeight document-wide — a silently weakened guard, major under the test-adequacy rubric.
